key_insight: Energy-based models provide a unifying lens for machine learning through three choices: energy function, inference procedure, and learning method.
engineering_relevance: This framework suggests new algorithms by swapping components and combining learned energies at inference time.
method: Define distributions as pθ(x) ∝ exp(−Eθ(x)), with energy determining what the model represents.
Connect sampling, variational inference, and learning objectives through a shared contrastive structure.
Map generative, discriminative, representation-learning, reinforcement-learning, and verifier-based methods into the same framework.
evidence_signal: The abstract presents a conceptual tutorial spanning many model families, but reports no datasets, quantitative benchmarks, or empirical comparisons.
watch_item: Practical tractability depends on how each formulation handles the partition function and sampling.
paper_title: An Energy-Based Perspective on Machine Learning
